summary: Discovery call focused on Meridian's embeddings + reranking needs for clinical search. Key concerns: vector DB integration, throughput/latency tradeoffs, dimensionality and index size, hybrid BM25 + embeddings approach, and security (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Redwood AE/SE explained Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and proposed pilot to measure throughput and rerank latencies with a cross-encoder step.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Wu (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Meridian Head of ML), Tom Blake (CTO), Ravi Patel (Infra), Emily Chen (PM)
Links shared: Redwood pilot deck (link), security-pack.pdf (link), benchmark-playbook.xlsx (link)

Summary: quick discovery to understand their search pipeline: currently BM25 + FAISS-ish setup, looking to add semantic layer and a rerank stage. Interested in Hosted vs Dedicated because of PHI/regulatory concerns.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Marcus who is our SE for search and embeddings. Could each of you intro quickly?
[00:12] Aisha Rahman: Hi, I'm Aisha, lead for ML at Meridian. We own the search models and signal pipeline.
[00:16] Tom Blake: Tom, CTO, oversight on infra and compliance.
[00:21] Ravi Patel: Ravi, infra eng, I handle the vector DBs and deployments.
[00:25] Emily Chen: Emily, PM, driving the use case — clinical documents search + QA.

[02:00] Marcus Wu: Great, thanks. Can you walk me through current architecture — what vector DB, dimensions, and QPS are you seeing?
[02:12] Ravi Patel: Sure. We currently ingest clinical notes into an internal FAISS cluster behind k8s, vectors are 768 dims from a transformer embedder we trained. Peak QPS for search is around 120 qps, but in production our 95th p99 latency target is 300ms for top-K retrieval. We then run a lightweight reranker that scores top-100 hits, but that's CPU-bound and slow.
[03:05] Marcus Wu: Ok, 768 dims and top-100 re-ranks — got it. Are you doing hybrid search (BM25 + vectors) today or pure vector?
[03:17] Aisha Rahman: We actually run BM25 first, then vector ANN on top of the BM25 filtered set for candidate mixing. It's a bit of a hack but gives better recall for clinical terms.
[03:30] Lena Ortiz: Makes sense. For your target latency and regulatory needs, we usually discuss three options: Hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool for you), or Private (VPC/on-prem). Tom, any compliance constraints?
[03:46] Tom Blake: Yeah, PHI is a concern. We need SOC2, encryption at rest, and ideally VPC peering or private link. We may prefer Dedicated or Private to avoid external multi-tenant exposure.
[04:05] Lena Ortiz: Understood. We have SOC2 Type II and can do VPC peering and dedicated instances; Private deploy is available for stricter environments. We'll send the security pack after this call.

[06:10] Marcus Wu: On the technical side for embeddings/rerank, do you want to do a two-stage pipeline? Typical pattern is ANN (like HNSW) to fetch ~200 candidates, then cross-encoder re-rank top-N (e.g., 10-50) to improve precision. That cross-encoder is the expensive part — usually run on GPU for low latency.
[06:35] Aisha Rahman: Yes, we like that pattern. Our current reranker is CPU only and can't scale at peak. What would Redwood recommend for dimensionality — is 768 fine, or should we move to 1536 for clinical domain?
[06:51] Marcus Wu: 768 is common and often sufficient, but clinical models sometimes benefit from larger embeddings (1k-1.5k). Tradeoffs: higher dims -> larger index size and slower ANN throughput, but potentially better semantic signal. We can benchmark both.
[07:10] Ravi Patel: Index size is a big deal for us. We're storing 40 million docs, so doubling dims affects memory and hosting costs.
[07:20] Marcus Wu: Right — with 40M docs, 768 dims at float32 is substantial; we usually recommend quantization (8-bit/4-bit) for storage and ANN-friendly formats. Redwood's Dedicated nodes support quantized models and KV cache for generators; for embeddings you can serve quantized vectors or compress indexes.

[09:05] Emily Chen: For rerank, do you suggest doing cross-encoder on every query or only for some?
[09:12] Marcus Wu: Often teams do ANN for recall, then cross-encoder for top-10 to top-50. Another pattern: do a cheap scoring heuristic first (BM25 + dot product) and only trigger cross-encoder when confidence is low or for high-value queries. That helps control cost and throughput.
[09:40] Aisha Rahman: Our traffic is mixed — a lot of low-value internal queries, but clinicians need high accuracy. So conditional reranking could be good.

[11:00] Lena Ortiz: Let's talk throughput numbers for a pilot. If you want p99 rerank latency under 500ms and we need to support bursts to 200 qps, we can size Dedicated GPUs accordingly or run Hosted with autoscale. Marcus, what would the approximate GPU footprint be for cross-encoder rerank of top-20 at 200 qps?
[11:25] Marcus Wu: Rough ballpark: a modern A10/A100-class GPU can serve cross-encoder rerank for that volume depending on batching and model quantization. If you batch effectively and use a smaller cross-encoder (distil or quantized), one or two GPUs can handle it. We'll put exact numbers in the benchmark playbook.
[11:47] Ravi Patel: Batching is tough because clinical queries need low latency; we can't batch across seconds. We need small batch sizes and short latency budgets.
[12:00] Marcus Wu: Understood — continuous batching with small micro-batches (2-8) can help. Redwood runtime supports micro-batching and automatic batching policies to improve throughput without blowing latencies.

[14:10] Tom Blake: What about embedding storage — do we need a separate vector DB or can Redwood host embeddings and provide search APIs that integrate with our BM25?
[14:25] Lena Ortiz: You have options. Many customers keep their vector DB (Pinecone, Milvus, FAISS) and call Redwood for embeddings + rerank GPU serving. Others move to Redwood Dedicated and let us host the index for a unified pipeline. Integration with your BM25 is straightforward — we accept hybrid candidate sets.
[14:50] Aisha Rahman: If we keep FAISS in-house, can Redwood call into our index or do we need to push vectors to Redwood?
[15:00] Marcus Wu: Redwood can do both. For Hosted mode, vectors typically reside with Redwood; for Dedicated/Private we can co-locate with your DB or call back into your private endpoint (with VPC peering). We'll architect the most secure path for PHI.

[17:20] Ravi Patel: Latency for retrieval from FAISS then rerank on Redwood — does network hop add too much?
[17:30] Marcus Wu: With VPC peering in Dedicated or Private deployments, network overhead is minimal (~a few ms). For Hosted (public API) we'd recommend replication in region or Dedicated to meet strict SLOs.

[20:00] Emily Chen: Anything about model versioning and rollouts? We need to test new embedder versions without breaking production.
[20:12] Lena Ortiz: Redwood supports model pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback. You can run A/B tests per route and compare recall/precision metrics over prompt sets. We also integrate with your eval suites.

[24:00] Aisha Rahman: Cost is big — cross-encoder on GPU adds up. How do you help optimize cost?
[24:12] Marcus Wu: We have Optimize tooling — suggestions for batching, quantization, and hybrid triggers. Eg, use ANN for 90% of queries, cross-encoder only for top-10 or high-value queries. We can show cost estimates in the pilot pricing.

[28:00] Tom Blake: Security again — KMS, HSM, audit logs?
[28:08] Lena Ortiz: Yes — KMS integration, optional HSM for Private, full audit logs per request, SSO/SAML and RBAC. We'll include those artifacts in the security pack.

[33:30] Marcus Wu: Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot ingesting a 500k document sample, run both 768 and 1536 embedders, run ANN recall tests, and measure rerank latencies with a cross-encoder on a Dedicated GPU. We'll provide a benchmark playbook and raw results.
[33:50] Emily Chen: That sounds good. What access do you need from us?
[33:55] Marcus Wu: Sample dataset, current vector schema, expected QPS profile, and a short list of eval queries / labeled relevance for ground truth. Also an infra contact for VPC peering if we go Dedicated.

[38:00] Aisha Rahman: Timeline — we want a pilot ASAP, ideally before end of month.
[38:10] Lena Ortiz: We'll send pilot SOW and pricing by 2026-11-15 and can kick off benchmarking the week after.

[42:00] Tom Blake: Anything else on SLAs?
[42:10] Lena Ortiz: Dedicated includes SLA options; Private deployments have enterprise SLAs and support. We'll include options in the SOW.

[47:00] Ravi Patel: One more question — embedding dimensionality and pruning: can Redwood provide tools to do PCA or product quantization?
[47:10] Marcus Wu: Yes, we have PQ pipelines and dimensionality reduction workflows as part of Optimize. We'll include recommended config and expected recall tradeoffs.

[51:00] Lena Ortiz: Great — recap: we will send pilot SOW + pricing + security pack by 2026-11-15; Marcus will prepare benchmark playbook; Ravi will send vector schema and QPS numbers; schedule technical deep-dive the week of 2026-11-22.
[51:20] Aisha Rahman: Thanks, that works.
[51:25] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and put everything in the CRM.

[55:00] Call ended

Notes on transcription: some ASR artifacts present (e.g., K-V cash for KV cache, FAIS vs FAISS spelled varyingly). Natural crosstalk occurred at 09:40 and 33:50.
